newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Natsionalny Rezervny Bank mulling ADR.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Natsionalny Rezervny Bank mulling ADR.

text.p: Russian investment bank Natsionalny Rezervny Bank is considering a public offering of international depositary receipts as well as a debt issue after it registers as a joint-stock bank in two months time, the head of the bank said on Thursday.

Bank Chairman Alexander Lebedev told Reuters the bank, one of Russia's top 10, would wait for international accountants Ernst & Young to finish an audit of its accounts before deciding what kind of paper to issue.
The bank, which is mostly owned by gas monopoly Gazprom, has already said it is considering issuing a Eurobond in 1997, but Lebedev said a commercial paper issue was also possible.

"This is still just a general idea; we will first finish changing the bank into a joint-stock bank and the next step will be possibly issuing some sort of paper -- maybe commercial maybe Eurobonds," Lebedev said.
Lebedev said any Eurobond issue by the bank, which is a major player in the market for former Soviet, or Vnesh, debt, would not be less than $100 million.

"It's very possible we will also make an international public offering of a part of our shares," Lebedev said, adding the bank could issue 10 percent of shares as American or Global Depositary Receipts. He said the bank's charter capital of five trillion roubles was almost complete. "(Five trillion) is a lot, so we want to go international," he said.
